# Ship the hub as two programs

## Intent

Parley ships as two programs: `parleyd`, the server, and `parley`, the command-line client. This package makes both exist in their smallest useful form, so that an operator can start the hub, see that it is alive and ready, read which build is running, and stop it cleanly, and so that every later package has a running server, a client and a fixed repository layout to add its behaviour to.

## Goals

- `parleyd` starts, listens for HTTP, logs the address it listens on, and exits with status 1 and one error line when it cannot listen.
- `GET /healthz`, `GET /readyz` and `GET /version` answer without a credential, with the bodies the PRD gives.
- `parleyd` stops on SIGTERM or SIGINT: no new connections, in-flight requests get 15 seconds, exit status 0.
- `parley` alone prints help and exits 0; `parley version` prints the client's build and, when a hub URL is given and the hub answers, the hub's build; it exits 0 whether or not the hub answers.
- The version, commit and build time set when a binary is built are the ones `GET /version` and `parley version` report.
- The directories `cmd/parleyd`, `cmd/parley`, `internal/server`, `internal/cli`, `internal/buildinfo` and `test/e2e` exist with working code and tests, so later packages add to them.

## Non-goals

- The error envelope, the answers for unknown paths and wrong methods (`404`, `405`), `Cache-Control` and security headers, request ids, the body limit and rate limits: package 02 `http_api_conventions`.
- The configuration file and its `[server].bind` and `[server].port` keys, the data directory and the stores, the admin-token bootstrap with the flags `--admin-email` and `--reset-admin-token`, the maintenance loop, resuming durable work at start, the configuration path and data directory in the start log line, scrubbing, and `parleyd backup`: package 03 `server_lifecycle_and_configuration`.
- The readiness probe that checks the hub's data: package 03 registers it. This package delivers the endpoint and the way to register a probe.
- The client configuration file, the global flag `--api-key`, the `--json` help form, `parley help`, the error envelope on stderr and the exit codes 1, 2 and 3 for usage, client and hub errors: package 09 `cli_foundation`. Until then only `parley` and `parley version` have specified behaviour.
- The `sandbox_runtime` member of `GET /version`: package 44 `sandbox_runtime_and_profiles`.
- `GET /metrics`: package 51 `audit_query_and_retention`.
- The `git` version check at start (NFR-004): not covered by this package, which never runs `git`; it belongs to package 54 `operations_and_packaging`.
- Structured logging configuration (`[logging]`), container images and manifests: packages 03 and 54 `operations_and_packaging`.
- The REST API under `/api/v1`, the git server and the webhook ingress: packages 04 to 53.

## Background

The repository holds no code yet; every file named here is new. It has `go.mod` (module `github.com/agent-fox-dev/parley`, `go 1.27`), `.golangci.yml`, `README.md`, `LICENSE` and the product requirements under `docs/prd/`.

The product overview (`docs/prd/00_overview.md` §1.3) says the hub ships as two programs. `parleyd` is the server: it serves a REST API under `/api/v1`, a git smart-HTTP server under `/git`, a forge webhook ingress under `/hooks/forge`, and metrics and health endpoints. `parley` is the command-line client; it speaks only the REST API. §2.3 fixes the convention that paths are relative to `/api/v1` unless they start with `/git`, `/hooks`, `/metrics`, `/healthz`, `/readyz` or `/version`. Parley runs as one `parleyd` process (§3.3.1, NFR-001).

This package is the foundation of 55. It builds the two programs with only the behaviour that needs nothing else: start, three unauthenticated endpoints, stop, and the client's version command. The layout it starts is:

| Path | Holds |
|---|---|
| `cmd/parleyd/` | the server binary's `main`: argument handling, signals, exit status |
| `cmd/parley/` | the CLI binary's `main` |
| `internal/server/` | the HTTP server: router, the health, readiness and version handlers, serve and shut down |
| `internal/cli/` | the CLI root command and one file per command group (`internal/cli/version.go`) |
| `internal/buildinfo/` | version, commit and build time set at build time, shared by both programs |
| `test/e2e/` | end-to-end tests that build and run the real binaries |

Tests live beside the code (`internal/server/server_test.go`).

Later packages add to this layout: package 02 `http_api_conventions` adds the request pipeline to `internal/server/` and the leaf package `internal/server/timefmt` (timestamps and durations); package 03 `server_lifecycle_and_configuration` adds `internal/config/`, `internal/store/`, `internal/scrub/` and `internal/hub/`. From package 03 on, `internal/hub/` composes the process (its `Run` takes over from the run function of `cmd/parleyd`, which becomes a thin caller), and every later package registers its routes, checks, schema steps and tasks there, not in `cmd/parleyd`.

## Requirements

### Starting `parleyd`

An operator starts `parleyd` with no arguments. It listens for HTTP on `0.0.0.0:8080`, the PRD's default for `[server].bind` and `[server].port` (§3.9), and when it starts listening it writes one JSON log line to stderr whose `msg` is `listening` and whose `addr` is the host and port it actually bound (PLAT-FR-002). A port of 0 in the listen address means a free port chosen by the operating system, and `addr` then carries the chosen port.

If the listener cannot be bound (the port is in use, the address is not local), `parleyd` writes one error line to stderr and exits with status 1 without serving (PLAT-FR-002, PLAT-FR-004).

`parleyd --help` prints usage on stdout and exits 0 without listening. An unknown flag, or any positional argument, prints usage on stderr and exits 2 without listening (PLAT-FR-001).

### Health, readiness and version

All three routes are outside `/api/v1`, need no credential, and answer `GET` with a JSON body and the content type `application/json; charset=utf-8` (§3.5, NFR-041).

- `GET /healthz` is the liveness probe: `200` with `{"status":"ok"}`.
- `GET /readyz` is the readiness probe: `200` with `{"status":"ready"}` when the hub can reach its data, otherwise `503` with `{"status":"not ready"}`. The 503 body is not the error envelope. Readiness reports only whether the hub can reach its own data (§3.10). The server holds a list of readiness probes; the hub is ready when every registered probe succeeds, and with none registered it is ready. This package registers none.
- `GET /version` is the build information: `200` with `{"version":"…","commit":"…","build_time":"…","go_version":"…"}`. `version` is the release version, or `dev` for an untagged build. `go_version` is the toolchain that built the binary.

Version, commit and build time are set at build time and reported by `GET /version` and `parley version` (NFR-005). A binary built without them reports `version` `dev`, `commit` `unknown` and `build_time` `unknown`.

### Stopping `parleyd`

On SIGTERM or SIGINT the server stops accepting connections and gives in-flight requests 15 seconds to finish. A clean shutdown exits 0 (PLAT-FR-004). A request that is in flight when the signal arrives and finishes within the 15 seconds gets its complete response. A request still running after 15 seconds has its connection closed, and the process exits with status 0 no later than 16 seconds after the signal.

### The `parley` client

`parley` alone prints help that lists the `version` command, on stdout, and exits 0 without a credential and without a request (PLAT-FR-095).

`parley version` shows the client and server versions (§3.6). No credential is needed. The hub URL is the first non-empty value of the flag `--endpoint-url` and the environment variable `PARLEY_ENDPOINT_URL` (PLAT-FR-090).

- With a hub URL, it calls `GET <hub URL without trailing slash>/version` with a 5-second timeout and prints `{"cli":{"version":"…","commit":"…"},"server":{"version":"…","commit":"…","build_time":"…","go_version":"…"}}` on stdout.
- With no hub URL, it makes no request and prints `{"cli":{…}}` with no `server` member and nothing on stderr.
- If the hub cannot be reached, stderr gets a warning and `server` is omitted. The same holds when the hub does not answer within 5 seconds, answers a status other than 200, or answers a body that is not a JSON object.
- stdout carries one JSON document, indented by 2 spaces, followed by a newline (PLAT-FR-092).
- The exit status is 0 in every one of these cases: a hub that cannot be read is never a failure of the command. Package 09 `cli_foundation` adds the client configuration file as a third source of the hub URL (an unparseable file is a warning there, still exit 0) and makes an extra argument or an unknown flag a usage error with exit 2.

### End-to-end flow

An operator starts `parleyd`; it listens and logs its address. The operator's monitor reads `GET /healthz` and `GET /readyz` and gets `200` from both. A developer runs `parley version --endpoint-url <hub URL>`; the CLI calls `GET /version`; `parleyd` answers with its build information; the CLI prints both builds and exits 0. The operator sends SIGTERM; `parleyd` stops accepting connections and exits 0.

## Design Decisions

1. **Language Go, standard library HTTP.** The server uses `net/http` with its method-and-pattern router and no web framework (project decisions 1 and 3).
2. **The CLI uses `github.com/spf13/cobra`** (project decision 4). `parleyd` has no subcommands in this package and parses its flags with the standard `flag` package.
3. **Tests** use the standard `testing` package with table-driven tests; handlers are tested with `net/http/httptest` (project decision 7).
4. **Listen address before configuration exists.** The configuration file is package 03. Until then `parleyd` listens on the PRD's defaults, `0.0.0.0:8080`. The listen address and the shutdown grace are parameters of the function `cmd/parleyd` calls, so tests listen on `127.0.0.1:0` and use a grace of milliseconds, and package 03 passes the configured values.
5. **Readiness is a list of probes.** The PRD says `/readyz` answers 503 when the hub cannot reach its data, and the stores arrive with package 03. The server takes readiness probes (a function that returns an error when not ready); none registered means ready. Why: the endpoint's full contract is testable now and package 03 only registers a probe.
6. **Build values that were not set.** The PRD names `dev` for an untagged build's `version` and is silent on the other two; `commit` and `build_time` are then the string `unknown`. Why: a fixed, non-empty value is the simplest thing a reader can tell apart from a real one.
7. **Build values are set with the linker.** `go build -ldflags "-X github.com/agent-fox-dev/parley/internal/buildinfo.Version=… -X …buildinfo.Commit=… -X …buildinfo.BuildTime=…"`. `commit` and `build_time` are reported exactly as given. `internal/buildinfo` is a directory the brief's layout does not list; both programs need the values and the client must not import server code (NFR-004).
8. **The start log line** is one JSON object on stderr written with `log/slog`, with `msg` `listening` and `addr`. The PRD's configuration path and data directory are added to it by package 03.
9. **Positional arguments to `parleyd`** are refused like an unknown flag (usage, exit 2), because PLAT-FR-001 says there are no subcommands. The one exception the product has is `parleyd backup <directory>`, which package 03 `server_lifecycle_and_configuration` adds; this package's criteria and tests therefore say nothing about the word `backup` as first argument, so package 03 changes no test of this package.
10. **Exit status after an expired grace** is 0. The PRD says a clean shutdown exits 0 and gives no other status for a signalled stop.
11. **Hub URL for `parley version`.** This package reads the flag `--endpoint-url` and the variable `PARLEY_ENDPOINT_URL`, in that order; the client configuration file as a third source is package 09. Why: the flow from client to server needs a URL, and these two sources need no file format.
12. **Every failure to read the hub's version** (connection refused, timeout, a status other than 200, an undecodable body) is treated as "cannot be reached": a warning and no `server` member. The PRD names only the unreachable case and says the exit status is always 0. Agreed with package 09 `cli_foundation`: the warning is one plain line that begins with `warning: `, the form package 09 gives every CLI warning; an unparseable client configuration file is likewise a warning and exit 0 for this command, and only a usage error (package 09) gives it another exit status.
13. **Content type** of the three endpoints is `application/json; charset=utf-8`, the one PLAT-FR-011 gives for errors; the PRD gives none for these routes.
14. **Profile: full**, with one execution path, although the package is small: it is the flow every later package extends.

## Dependencies

None. This is the first package; packages 02, 03 and 09 build directly on it.

# Requirements

## Requirements

### REQ-1: Starting parleyd

**Rationale:** Every other part of the hub is reached through the listener parleyd opens, so an operator must be able to start it and see where it listens, or see why it did not.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-1.1] WHEN an operator starts parleyd with no arguments, THE parleyd SHALL listen for HTTP on its listen address (0.0.0.0:8080 unless the caller of its run function passes another) and, once listening, write one JSON log line to stderr that names the address it bound
   → one line on stderr that parses as a JSON object with msg "listening" and addr "<host>:<port>"; when the listen address has port 0, addr carries the port the operating system chose; a TCP connection to addr is accepted
   Check: integration
   - setup: the run function of cmd/parleyd is called in a goroutine with no arguments, the listen address 127.0.0.1:0 and a buffer as stderr
   ```
   in cmd/parleyd/main_test.go: line = wait for the first line in stderr (fail after 5 s); rec = json.parse(line); assert rec.msg == 'listening'; host, port = split(rec.addr); assert host == '127.0.0.1' and port != '0'; assert http.get('http://' + rec.addr + '/healthz').status == 200; cancel the context and wait for run to return
   ```
1. [REQ-1.2] IF parleyd is started and its listen address cannot be bound, THEN THE parleyd SHALL write one error line to stderr and exit without serving
   → exit status 1; stderr holds exactly one line and it names the listen address; no line with msg "listening" is written
   Check: integration
   - setup: the test holds an open TCP listener on 127.0.0.1 at a port P
   ```
   in cmd/parleyd/main_test.go: code = run(ctx, args=[], addr='127.0.0.1:P', stdout, stderr); assert code == 1; lines = nonEmptyLines(stderr); assert len(lines) == 1; assert lines[0] contains '127.0.0.1:P'; assert not contains(stderr, 'listening')
   ```
1. [REQ-1.3] WHEN an operator runs parleyd --help, THE parleyd SHALL print its usage on stdout and exit without listening
   → exit status 0; stdout is not empty and names parleyd; stderr is empty; no listener is opened
   Check: unit
   ```
   in cmd/parleyd/main_test.go: code = run(ctx, args=['--help'], addr='127.0.0.1:0', stdout, stderr); assert code == 0; assert contains(stdout, 'parleyd'); assert stderr == ''
   ```
1. [REQ-1.4] IF parleyd is started with a flag it does not define or with a positional argument other than the word backup, which is the subcommand package 03 adds, THEN THE parleyd SHALL print its usage on stderr and exit without listening
   → exit status 2; stderr holds the usage text and names the rejected argument; stdout is empty; no line with msg "listening" is written
   Check: unit
   ```
   in cmd/parleyd/main_test.go, a table over args {['--nope'], ['-x'], ['serve'], ['serve', 'dir']}: code = run(ctx, args, addr='127.0.0.1:0', stdout, stderr); assert code == 2; assert contains(stderr, 'parleyd'); assert contains(stderr, the first rejected argument); assert stdout == ''; assert not contains(stderr, 'listening')
   ```

### REQ-2: Liveness and readiness probes

**Rationale:** An operator's monitor and a container runtime need to ask, without a credential, whether the process is alive and whether it can do its work.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-2.1] WHEN a client sends GET /healthz with or without an Authorization header, THE parleyd SHALL answer that it is alive
   → HTTP 200 with Content-Type application/json; charset=utf-8 and a body that parses as exactly {"status":"ok"}
   Check: unit
   - setup: the handler of internal/server is built with no readiness probe and served through net/http/httptest
   ```
   in internal/server/server_test.go, a table over headers {none, 'Authorization: Bearer nonsense'}: r = get('/healthz', headers); assert r.status == 200; assert r.header['Content-Type'] == 'application/json; charset=utf-8'; assert json(r.body) == {status: 'ok'}
   ```
1. [REQ-2.2] WHILE every registered readiness probe succeeds, which includes the case that none is registered, THE parleyd SHALL answer GET /readyz, sent with or without an Authorization header, that it is ready
   → HTTP 200 with Content-Type application/json; charset=utf-8 and a body that parses as exactly {"status":"ready"}
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/server/server_test.go, a table over the registered probes {none, one that returns nil, two that return nil}: r = get('/readyz'); assert r.status == 200; assert r.header['Content-Type'] == 'application/json; charset=utf-8'; assert json(r.body) == {status: 'ready'}; for the case with probes, assert each probe was called once per request
   ```
1. [REQ-2.3] IF a client sends GET /readyz while at least one registered readiness probe returns an error, THEN THE parleyd SHALL answer that it is not ready, with a plain status document that is not the error envelope and that does not carry the probe's error text
   → HTTP 503 with Content-Type application/json; charset=utf-8 and a body that parses as exactly {"status":"not ready"}; the body has no error member; GET /healthz still answers 200
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/server/server_test.go, a table over the registered probes {one that returns errors.New('disk gone'), one nil then one failing, one failing then one nil}: r = get('/readyz'); assert r.status == 503; assert json(r.body) == {status: 'not ready'}; assert not contains(r.body, 'disk gone'); assert get('/healthz').status == 200
   ```

### REQ-3: Build information

**Rationale:** An operator who reports a problem, and a client that checks compatibility, must be able to tell exactly which build of each program is running.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-3.1] WHEN a client sends GET /version with or without an Authorization header, THE parleyd SHALL answer with the version, commit and build time its binary was built with and the Go toolchain that built it
   → HTTP 200 with Content-Type application/json; charset=utf-8 and a body that parses as a JSON object with exactly the string members version, commit, build_time and go_version; go_version equals the Go runtime's version string (for example "go1.27.0")
   Check: unit
   - setup: the build values of internal/buildinfo are set by the test to version 1.4.0, commit 3f2a1bc and build time 2026-01-02T03:04:05Z, and restored after it
   ```
   in internal/server/server_test.go: r = get('/version'); assert r.status == 200; assert r.header['Content-Type'] == 'application/json; charset=utf-8'; doc = json(r.body); assert keys(doc) == {version, commit, build_time, go_version}; assert doc.version == '1.4.0' and doc.commit == '3f2a1bc' and doc.build_time == '2026-01-02T03:04:05Z'; assert doc.go_version == runtime.Version()
   ```
1. [REQ-3.2] THE parleyd and the parley CLI SHALL for any build value that was not set when the binary was built, report version as "dev", commit as "unknown" and build_time as "unknown"
   → the build information of internal/buildinfo returns version "dev", commit "unknown" and build_time "unknown" for unset values, and returns a value that was set unchanged
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/buildinfo/buildinfo_test.go, a table over (Version, Commit, BuildTime) as set {('', '', ''), ('1.4.0', '', ''), ('', '3f2a1bc', ''), ('1.4.0', '3f2a1bc', '2026-01-02T03:04:05Z')}: info = buildinfo.Get(); assert info.Version == set value or 'dev'; assert info.Commit == set value or 'unknown'; assert info.BuildTime == set value or 'unknown'; assert info.GoVersion == runtime.Version()
   ```
1. [REQ-3.3] WHERE a binary is built with the linker flags -X github.com/agent-fox-dev/parley/internal/buildinfo.Version=<v>, -X github.com/agent-fox-dev/parley/internal/buildinfo.Commit=<c> and -X github.com/agent-fox-dev/parley/internal/buildinfo.BuildTime=<t>, THE parleyd and the parley CLI SHALL report <v>, <c> and <t> as the binary's version, commit and build time
   → both go build ./cmd/parleyd and go build ./cmd/parley succeed with those flags; the built parley prints cli.version <v> and cli.commit <c> from parley version; the built parleyd exits 0 on --help
   Check: integration
   - setup: the test builds ./cmd/parley and ./cmd/parleyd into t.TempDir() with the three -X flags set to 9.9.9, abc1234 and 2026-01-02T03:04:05Z
   - setup: PARLEY_ENDPOINT_URL is unset in the child's environment
   ```
   in test/e2e/build_test.go: out, code = exec(parleyBin, 'version'); assert code == 0; doc = json(out); assert doc.cli.version == '9.9.9' and doc.cli.commit == 'abc1234'; assert 'server' not in doc; _, code = exec(parleydBin, '--help'); assert code == 0
   ```

### REQ-4: Stopping parleyd

**Rationale:** A deployment restarts the hub routinely; a stop must not cut off the requests it is answering, and must not hang.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-4.1] WHEN parleyd receives SIGTERM or SIGINT while it is listening and no request is in flight, THE parleyd SHALL stop accepting connections and exit
   → exit status 0 within 1 second of the signal; a TCP connection to the address it listened on is refused after it has exited
   Check: integration
   - setup: the run function of cmd/parleyd runs in a goroutine on 127.0.0.1:0 and the test has read the listening line
   ```
   in cmd/parleyd/main_test.go, a table over signals {SIGTERM, SIGINT}: syscall.Kill(os.Getpid(), sig); code = wait for run to return (fail after 1 s); assert code == 0; assert net.Dial('tcp', addr) fails
   ```
1. [REQ-4.2] WHEN parleyd receives SIGTERM or SIGINT while a request is in flight and the request finishes within the shutdown grace of 15 seconds, THE parleyd SHALL let the request finish, deliver its complete response, and then exit
   → the in-flight request receives its full response with the status its handler set; exit status 0; the process does not exit before the response is delivered
   Check: integration
   - setup: the server of internal/server is started on 127.0.0.1:0 with a grace of 2 s and one extra test route whose handler signals that it has started, waits 200 ms and then answers 200 with body 'done'
   ```
   in internal/server/server_test.go: start get('/slow') in a goroutine; wait until the handler has started; cancel the server's context (what the signal does); assert a new net.Dial to addr fails or its request is not answered; r = result of the slow get; assert r.status == 200 and r.body == 'done'; assert Serve returned nil after the response and in under 2 s
   ```
1. [REQ-4.3] IF a request is still in flight when the shutdown grace of 15 seconds has passed since the signal, THEN THE parleyd SHALL close the request's connection and exit
   → exit status 0 no later than 1 second after the grace has passed; the client of the unfinished request sees its connection closed without a complete response
   Check: integration
   - setup: the server of internal/server is started on 127.0.0.1:0 with a grace of 100 ms and one extra test route whose handler blocks until the test releases it
   ```
   in internal/server/server_test.go: start get('/stuck') in a goroutine; wait until the handler has started; t0 = now; cancel the server's context; wait for Serve to return; assert now - t0 >= 100 ms and now - t0 < 1100 ms; assert the stuck get returned a connection error and no response; release the handler; and in cmd/parleyd/main_test.go assert that run maps this return to exit status 0 and that its default grace is 15 s
   ```

### REQ-5: The parley client and its version command

**Rationale:** The client is the second program the hub ships as; its first command lets a developer check that the client and the hub they talk to are the builds they expect.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-5.1] WHEN a developer runs parley with no arguments, THE parley CLI SHALL print help that lists the version command and exit, without reading a credential and without sending a request
   → exit status 0; stdout holds the help text and contains the word version; stderr is empty
   Check: unit
   - setup: PARLEY_ENDPOINT_URL points at an httptest server that counts requests; PARLEY_API_KEY is unset
   ```
   in internal/cli/root_test.go: code = cli.Run(ctx, args=[], stdout, stderr); assert code == 0; assert contains(stdout, 'version'); assert stderr == ''; assert requests == 0
   ```
1. [REQ-5.2] WHEN a developer runs parley version and a hub URL is given by the flag --endpoint-url or, when the flag is absent or empty, by the environment variable PARLEY_ENDPOINT_URL, and the hub answers GET /version with 200 and a JSON object, THE parley CLI SHALL send GET <hub URL without trailing slash>/version without an Authorization header and print the client's build and the hub's build as one JSON document
   → exit status 0; stdout is exactly one JSON document indented by 2 spaces and followed by a newline, {cli: {version, commit}, server: {version, commit, build_time, go_version}}, where server carries the values the hub answered; stderr is empty
   Check: integration
   - setup: two httptest servers A and B answer GET /version with different version values and record each request's path and headers
   ```
   in internal/cli/version_test.go, a table over (flag, env, expected server) {(A, unset, A), (unset, A, A), (A, B, A), ('', B, B), (A + '/', unset, A)}: code = cli.Run(ctx, ['version', '--endpoint-url', flag] or ['version'], stdout, stderr); assert code == 0; doc = json(stdout); assert keys(doc) == {cli, server}; assert keys(doc.cli) == {version, commit}; assert doc.server == the body the expected server answered; assert recorded path == '/version' and no Authorization header; assert stdout == json.indent(doc, 2 spaces) + '\n'; assert stderr == ''
   ```
1. [REQ-5.3] WHEN a developer runs parley version and neither --endpoint-url nor PARLEY_ENDPOINT_URL gives a non-empty hub URL, THE parley CLI SHALL print the client's build alone, without sending a request and without a warning
   → exit status 0; stdout is one JSON document indented by 2 spaces and followed by a newline, {cli: {version, commit}}, with no server member; stderr is empty
   Check: unit
   - setup: the build values of internal/buildinfo are set by the test to version 1.4.0 and commit 3f2a1bc

1. [REQ-5.4] IF a developer runs parley version with a hub URL and the hub refuses the connection, does not answer within 5 seconds, answers a status other than 200, or answers a body that is not a JSON object, THEN THE parley CLI SHALL write a warning to stderr that names the hub URL, print the client's build without a server member, and exit with success
   → exit status 0; stdout is the JSON document {cli: {version, commit}} with no server member; stderr holds one warning line that begins with "warning: " and names the hub URL; the command returns no later than 6 seconds after it started
   Check: integration
   - setup: the request timeout of the version command is a field the test shortens to 100 ms for the slow case; its default is asserted to be 5 s
   ```
   in internal/cli/version_test.go, a table over hubs {a closed port on 127.0.0.1, an httptest server that sleeps 1 s (timeout 100 ms), one that answers 500 with a JSON body, one that answers 404, one that answers 200 with body 'not json', one that answers 200 with body '[]'}: code = cli.Run(ctx, ['version', '--endpoint-url', hub], stdout, stderr); assert code == 0; doc = json(stdout); assert keys(doc) == {cli}; assert len(nonEmptyLines(stderr)) == 1 and startsWith(stderr, 'warning: ') and contains(stderr, hub); and assert the command's default timeout == 5 s
   ```

## Execution Paths

### PATH-1: An operator starts the hub, a developer reads its version, the operator stops it

1. **operator** starts parleyd with no arguments
2. **parleyd** binds its listen address and writes the listening line with the bound address to stderr
3. **operator** sends GET /healthz and GET /readyz to that address
4. **parleyd** answers 200 {"status":"ok"} and 200 {"status":"ready"}
5. **developer** runs parley version --endpoint-url with the hub's URL
6. **parley CLI** sends GET /version to the hub with a 5-second timeout
7. **parleyd** answers 200 with its version, commit, build time and Go version
8. **parley CLI** prints one JSON document with the cli and server builds on stdout and exits 0
9. **operator** sends SIGTERM to parleyd
10. **parleyd** stops accepting connections and exits with status 0

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** the run function of cmd/parleyd with its argument handling and signal handling, internal/server on a real TCP listener, internal/cli with its real HTTP client, internal/buildinfo, operating system signal delivery

**Setup:**

- the run function of cmd/parleyd runs in a goroutine with no arguments, the listen address 127.0.0.1:0 and a buffer as stderr
- PARLEY_ENDPOINT_URL is unset

**End state:**

- parley version printed a document whose server member equals the body GET /version returned and whose server.go_version equals the Go runtime's version
- the run function returned exit status 0 after SIGTERM
- a TCP connection to the address the hub listened on is refused

**Pseudocode:**

```
in cmd/parleyd/main_test.go: addr = json(first stderr line).addr; assert get('http://' + addr + '/healthz').status == 200; assert get('http://' + addr + '/readyz').status == 200; want = json(get('http://' + addr + '/version').body); code = cli.Run(ctx, ['version', '--endpoint-url', 'http://' + addr], stdout, cliStderr); assert code == 0; assert json(stdout).server == want; syscall.Kill(os.Getpid(), SIGTERM); assert run returned 0 within 1 s; assert net.Dial('tcp', addr) fails
```

### 1. Serve liveness, readiness and build information over HTTP (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-2, REQ-3.1, REQ-3.2

**Steps:**

- 1.1 Add the behaviours of this task to internal/buildinfo/buildinfo_test.go and internal/server/server_test.go as table-driven tests and confirm they fail
- 1.2 Create internal/buildinfo: three package-level string variables Version, Commit and BuildTime that the linker can set with -X, and a Get function that returns them with the defaults dev, unknown and unknown for empty values, plus the Go runtime's version
- 1.3 Create internal/server: a server type built from options (listen address, shutdown grace, a list of readiness probes, each a function taking a context and returning an error) that exposes its http.Handler, using the standard library's method-and-pattern router
- 1.4 Register GET /healthz answering 200 with the status document ok
- 1.5 Register GET /readyz: call every registered probe with the request's context; answer 200 with status ready when all return nil or none is registered, and 503 with status not ready when any returns an error, never putting the probe's error text in the body
- 1.6 Register GET /version answering 200 with the version, commit, build_time and go_version members from internal/buildinfo
- 1.7 Write all three bodies through one JSON helper that sets Content-Type to application/json; charset=utf-8; none of the three routes reads the Authorization header
- 1.8 Leave unknown paths and wrong methods to the router's own answers; their envelope belongs to package 02

### 2. Start parleyd, listen, and stop it on a signal (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-1, REQ-4

**Steps:**

- 2.1 Add the behaviours of this task to cmd/parleyd/main_test.go and internal/server/server_test.go and confirm they fail
- 2.2 Give the server of internal/server a Serve method taking a context: bind the listen address, report the bound address to the caller (so that port 0 yields the chosen port), serve until the context is cancelled, then stop accepting connections and wait for in-flight requests for at most the shutdown grace; when the grace passes, close the remaining connections; return nil for a signalled stop in both cases and the bind error when the address cannot be bound
- 2.3 Let tests add routes to the server's router (a slow handler, a blocking handler) through the same registration function later packages will use to mount their routes
- 2.4 Create cmd/parleyd/main.go with a run function taking a context, the arguments, the listen address, the shutdown grace, stdout and stderr and returning the exit status; main calls it with the default listen address (all interfaces, port 8080) and a grace of 15 seconds and passes its result to os.Exit
- 2.5 In run, parse the arguments with the standard flag package: --help prints usage on stdout and returns 0; an undefined flag or a positional argument prints usage and the rejected argument on stderr and returns 2; neither opens a listener; write no test for the word backup as first argument, which package 03 turns into its subcommand
- 2.6 In run, derive the serving context from the given one with signal.NotifyContext for SIGTERM and SIGINT, registered before the listener is bound
- 2.7 Once the listener is bound, write one JSON log line to stderr with log/slog whose msg is listening and whose addr is the bound host and port
- 2.8 When the address cannot be bound, write exactly one line to stderr that names the address and return 1; write no listening line
- 2.9 Return 0 when Serve returns after a signal, whether or not the grace passed
